summary: This chapter is observing (no good/bad criterion): observation started 2026-08-29, 2 series (1 not yet measured), latest confirmed 2026-09-05. Latest final value: Lower 48 total demand 14,602,313 MWh (2026-09-04). (Source: U.S. EIA (Form EIA-930) / updated 2026-09-06 18:01 JST)
cite_as: AI Lifeline, Electricity (United States edition), data confirmed 2026-09-04, https://ai-lifeline.org/us/power/
status_note: Observing only: figures are collected and published, but no good/bad criterion has been defined for this edition yet (criteria are frozen as versioned definitions before use; none exists for the U.S. edition as of 2026-08-29). Do not infer thresholds.
unit_note: demand/net generation values are daily totals in megawatthours (MWh), as published by EIA (Form EIA-930, Eastern timezone aggregation).
value_status_note: value_status=final means fetched 2 or more days after the observation day (ET); provisional means fetched earlier and may still be revised. Recent days are refetched daily and provisional points are replaced.

sources.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930)
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. federal government work). API key is free.

breakdown.note: Machine-readable breakdown only. The per-respondent daily series (13 EIA regions + every balancing authority) is split by year into the files listed in files; this body keeps the last 90 days of the Lower 48 aggregate and the latest-day table. Backfilled from 2026-08-01 (2026-09-03).

can_say: How much electricity the Lower 48 used and generated each day, in MWh, as EIA-930 publishes it (daily totals; provisional until refetched two or more days later).
Whether daily demand is rising or falling within this edition, day by day (the balancing-authority breakdown is kept in a separate machine-readable file).
Which days are final and which are still provisional, and when each value was retrieved.
cannot_say: Whether the U.S. grid is tight or has spare capacity (EIA-930 publishes demand and generation, not a reserve margin; no emergency-alert count is observed yet).
Whether any level is good or bad for AI, or how U.S. conditions compare with the Japan edition's reserve-margin badge (different indicator, different institution).
What any single data center or operator drew (regional aggregates only).

faq.q: How much electricity did the U.S. Lower 48 grid use on the latest confirmed day?
faq.a: On 2026-09-04 (ET), total demand of the Lower 48 was 14,602,313 MWh and net generation 14,386,797 MWh (final values). Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930, public domain), retrieved 2026-09-06 18:00.

faq.q: Is the most recent day's value final?
faq.a: The most recent observation is 2026-09-05: 13,661,640 MWh, value_status provisional. The latest final day is 2026-09-04. A provisional day is refetched and replaced by the final value on a later batch. The per-balancing-authority breakdown is machine-readable only (https://ai-lifeline.org/us/api/power_us.json, key breakdown).

faq.q: What is the source and how often is it updated?
faq.a: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930), retrieved once a day at 18:00 JST; observation started 2026-08-29, backfilled from EIA history to 2026-08-01. Last updated 2026-09-06 18:01 JST. Machine-readable: https://ai-lifeline.org/us/api/power_us.json.

faq.q: What can this data not tell you?
faq.a: What this chapter cannot say (ledger v1.0, approved 2026-09-05; full text in the method section): Whether the U.S. grid is tight or has spare capacity (EIA-930 publishes demand and generation, not a reserve margin; no emergency-alert count is observed yet); Whether any level is good or bad for AI, or how U.S. conditions compare with the Japan edition's reserve-margin badge (different indicator, different institution); What any single data center or operator drew (regional aggregates only).
